import html # Predefined HTML template with placeholders for the event invitation. INVITATION_FORMAT = """ {title} - Invitation

{title}

{description}
Date: {date}
{notes_block}
""" def generate_event_invite(title: str, description: str, date: str, notes: str) -> str: """ Generate a sanitized HTML invitation for an event. Parameters ---------- title : str The name or title of the event. description : str A comprehensive description of the event (may contain multiple lines and formatting). date : str The scheduled date for the event. notes : str Extra information or instructions provided by the user. Returns ------- str A string containing sanitized HTML for safely displaying the event invitation. Raises ------ ValueError If any of the required arguments are empty strings. """ # Basic validation: ensure mandatory fields are provided if not title.strip(): raise ValueError("Title cannot be empty.") if not description.strip(): raise ValueError("Description cannot be empty.") if not date.strip(): raise ValueError("Date cannot be empty.") # Escape user-provided content to prevent HTML injection (CWE-74) safe_title = html.escape(title, quote=True) safe_description = html.escape(description, quote=False).replace("\n", "
") safe_date = html.escape(date, quote=True) # Notes are optional; if provided, escape and wrap in a styled div notes_block = "" if notes.strip(): safe_notes = html.escape(notes, quote=False).replace("\n", "
") notes_block = f'
{safe_notes}
' # Render the final HTML using the predefined template return INVITATION_FORMAT.format( title=safe_title, description=safe_description, date=safe_date, notes_block=notes_block )
